title: Dedicated capacity overlay SKU bundles: fault-tolerant burst + SLA granularity
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Propose a compact set of 'overlay bundles' for Dedicated capacity that combine reserved GPU commitments with measured burst credits, soft autoscale guardrails, and tiered SLAs. Goal is to simplify enterprise procurement conversations and reduce configuration confusion while protecting platform SLOs and preserving margins.

Background: Sales feedback and contract reviews show customers are overwhelmed by fine-grained commit options and separate burst/credits contracts. Engineering operability notes show several near-miss incidents when customers attempted ad-hoc bursting which bypassed guardrails. Current catalog (many small SKUs + custom deals) slows legal review and increases quoting cycles.

Hypothesis: Packaging reserved units into three opinionated overlay bundles (Starter, Business, Resilience) with built-in burst buffers and defined autoscale rules will reduce sales cycle length by >=20%, increase attach-rate of burst add-ons by 30%, and reduce incident risk from uncontrolled bursting.

Proposed bundle sketches (examples only):
- Starter: 4 reserved GPUs, 1.5x burst credit pool (30 min sustained equivalent), soft SLA (98.7% p99 latency), limited autoscale to +1 node.
- Business: 16 reserved GPUs, 2.0x burst credits, standard SLA (99.5% p99), autoscale to +25% sustained for short windows, prioritized routing in regional pools.
- Resilience: 64 reserved GPUs, 3.0x burst credits, enterprise SLA (99.95% p99), cross-region failover, on-call escalation credits, optional HSM/KMS bundle.

Key design elements:
- Burst credits measured in GPU-minutes, consumed from an overlay pool with depletion alarms and automatic throttling fallback to lower-tier model variants rather than total request rejection.
- Autoscale guardrails: per-customer rate limits and cooldown windows encoded in the Dedicated control plane; explicit contract terms for preemption and graceful degradation.
- SLA granularity: tiered p99 latency and availability commitments with financial remediation bands; binary eligibility rules (e.g., minimum reserved units required for Resilience).
- Quoting simplification: single-line item per bundle in SOW with optional add-ons (extra burst credit bags, priority support, dedicated infra manager).

Measurement plan: run A/B pilot with 6 enterprise prospects (3 current customers testing Business bundle, 3 new trials on Starter) over 12 weeks. Track sales cycle time, conversion %, burst attach rate, number of burst-related incidents, and modeled unit economics (net margin per GPU-hour). Success criteria defined below.

Risks and mitigations:
- Margin erosion if burst usage consistently high -> mitigation: dynamic pricing floor and overage tiers + quota notifications.
- Complexity in billing and observability -> mitigation: new Console UI card showing burst pool consumption and automatic alerts integrated with billing dashboards.
- Legal/security requirements (on-prem/VPC customers) -> require Security Questionnaire and potential carve-outs; legal to standardize contract language.

Deliverables: Confluence PRD, pilot pricing spreadsheet, contract language template, Console prototype for burst visibility, implementation scope doc with ENG, gating checklist for security review.
acceptance_criteria: Pilot executed with 6 customers and weekly usage snapshots captured for 12 weeks
Sales cycle time measured and compared to baseline with >=20% reduction target
Pricing spreadsheet includes modeled net margin per bundle and overage rules validated by finance
Console shows live burst pool consumption and threshold alerts; Beta UI validated by pilot customers
Legal and Security sign-off on SOW language for all three bundles and documented exceptions
